text:
maya: Heads-up — I pushed a draft Grafana panel for GPU SLO burn-rate by cluster. Link: https://grafana.redwood/d/abcd123
maya: Panel aggregates error-budget burn over 1h and splits by cluster + model_type. It's super noisy — cardinality explodes because of instance_id and experiment_id labels.
jared: Nice. Can you paste the PromQL you're using?
maya: PromQL:
```
sum by(cluster) (increase(gpu_slo_errors_total[1h])) / sum by(cluster) (increase(gpu_slo_requests_total[1h]))
```
maya: I originally had `by(cluster, instance_id)` which produced ~400 series and made the panel useless.
li: Try dropping instance_id earlier or use label_replace to normalize. e.g.:
```
label_replace(gpu_slo_requests_total, "instance", "", "instance", "(.*)")
```
li: or simpler: `sum without(instance_id) (increase(...))` depending on your metric shape.
samir: Another approach is to present a topk(10) view and a separate "others" series, so UI isn't overwhelmed. Also consider smoothing with `avg_over_time(...[10m])` for the visual.
noor: For alerts, we should avoid cluster-level noise. Proposed: alert when burn_rate(cluster,30m) > 0.02 AND requests(cluster,30m) > 1k. Otherwise it's noise from low-volume clusters.
monitoring-bot: Alert: GPU_SLO_BURN firing — cluster=eu-west3 — burn_rate=0.031 (30m)
maya: Saw that. The panel should show both instantaneous and baseline (30d rolling) so ops can tell if it's transient.
jared: Suggest computing a request-weighted burn rate so one noisy instance doesn't dominate: `sum(increase(errors[1h])) by (cluster) / sum(increase(requests[1h])) by (cluster)` then use `or on(cluster) group_left() vector(0)` to keep zero-series.
li: Also add a dashboard variable for `cluster` and `service` to let folks drill down. In the legend, show `{{cluster}} (series: {{__series_count}})` — Grafana can expose series count via Transform if needed.
noor: Can we add a derived "cardinality_noise" metric: `count_values("series", gpu_latency_count_total)` grouped by cluster+model_type and surface warning when >200 unique series? That would let us flag panels that need aggregation.
maya: Good idea. I'll add a hidden stat panel that computes unique series per cluster and annotate the main graph when it exceeds threshold. Also planning to cap displayed series to top 12 by traffic and fold the rest into "other".
samir: If we cap series, add a short markdown note explaining that non-top series are grouped to avoid skew. Otherwise folks will chase missing traffic.
maya: I'll push a dashboard JSON update with the new panel and alert tweaks. Rollout plan: internal preview 9am PST tomorrow, then org-wide. @jared can you review the alert thresholds and promql?
jared: Will review now for a quick pass, deeper review tomorrow morning. A couple quick notes: use `increase(...[30m])` for alert window, and avoid `rate()` on counter resets for long windows.
monitoring-bot: Deploy job `grafana/dashboard/update` succeeded for dashboard id=1124 at 2024-11-05T16:02:23Z
maya: Thanks all — I'll follow up with the PR link once deployed. :thumbsup:
jared: Quick UX note: show sparkline + latest value column so paging on the team page is easier. :eyes:
